results: 1. I will swing the tendon hammer towards your other limbs, stopping short, to see if they jerk too.
anticipatory jerk to a feigned tendon-hammer approach (Hallett sign): POSITIVE - the jerk occurs when the hammer is stopped just short of the tendon, provoked by the visual stimulus alone
2. I will test your reflexes the normal way, tapping the tendon, on both arms and legs.
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
3. I will test the tone in your arms and legs by passively flexing and extending them.
4. I will test power in all four limbs against resistance.
MRC power in all four limbs: 5/5 throughout
5. I will test sensation to light touch, pinprick, and vibration in all four limbs.
6. I will perform a fundoscopy to examine the back of your eyes.
7. I will perform a Slit-lamp examination of the anterior segment of your eyes.
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder (functional movement disorder presenting as a non-organic reflex jerk / Hallett's sign)

Alternative 1: Hyperthyroidism or other cause of neuromuscular hyper-excitability
Alternative 2: Subtle / pre-symptomatic corticospinal tract lesion (e.g. early multiple sclerosis or motor neuron disease)
Alternative 3: Hypocalcaemia or other metabolic cause of reflex hyperexcitability
